Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
" *

Copies the given array and adds the given element at the end of the new array.

* *

The new array contains the same elements of the input * array plus the given element in the last position. The component type of * the new array is the same as that of the input array.

* *

If the input array is null, a new one element array is returned * whose component type is the same as the element, unless the element itself is null, * in which case the return type is Object[]

* * 
     * ArrayUtils.add(null, null)      = [null]
     * ArrayUtils.add(null, "a")       = ["a"]
     * ArrayUtils.add(["a"], null)     = ["a", null]
     * ArrayUtils.add(["a"], "b")      = ["a", "b"]
     * ArrayUtils.add(["a", "b"], "c") = ["a", "b", "c"]
     *
* * @param array the array to "add" the element to, may be null * @param element the object to add, may be null * @return A new array containing the existing elements plus the new element * The returned array type will be that of the input array (unless null), * in which case it will have the same type as the element. * If both are null, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown * @since 2.1 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if both arguments are null "

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test asserts: In org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtilsAddTest.testLANG571(), both arguments to ArrayUtils.add are null. The test expects an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown.
- What the code does: In org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T) (lines 3288–3301):
  - It determines a component type via:
    - if (array != null) type = array.getClass();
    - else if (element != null) type = element.getClass();
    - else type = Object.class;  // when both are null (lines 3292–3295)
  - It then calls copyArrayGrow1(array, type), which for a null array returns a new array of newArrayComponentType with length 1 (lines 3528–3536), i.e., a new Object[1].
  - No exception is thrown; it returns Object[] containing a single null.
- Why the test fails: Because the method returns an Object[] instead of throwing an IllegalArgumentException, the test’s fail(...) is reached and the expected exception is not thrown.
- Why this is a bug beyond the test: The method’s own Javadoc states: “If both are null, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown” and warns that otherwise a null/null call would yield Object[]. Returning Object[] here can also surface as a ClassCastException at runtime when the generic return type T[] is inferred (e.g., String[]), but the actual object is Object[]; the implicit checkcast at the call site fails, matching the issue report.
- Root cause: Missing explicit guard for the “both parameters are null” case in ArrayUtils.add(T[], T). The current else branch chooses Object.class and proceeds to create and return an Object[] rather than throwing the documented IllegalArgumentException.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
